text:
Trees move. Give the rope a spring.

Trees move in the wind, and they move apart. A rope sagging ten percent goes straight once its trees lean apart 34 centimetres; at five percent, after only 8.5. After that the rope stretches, and every further centimetre adds about 4 kilonewtons. So the deep sag earns its keep twice, and the X still gets a heavy spring at every end, to let it give.
